# useRef vs useState — mutable values that do not re-render

> Two counters side by side: state re-renders on every click, a ref changes silently and is read from a handler.

🟢 beginner · React 16.8+ · Built-in Hooks › Refs & identity · support: universal

**Playground:** `npm run dev` → [`#/entry/use-ref-vs-state`](http://localhost:5173/#/entry/use-ref-vs-state)

## Concept

State is a snapshot that triggers a re-render when set. A ref is a mutable box: writing `ref.current` is immediate, never re-renders, and the latest value is visible to every handler.

## Problem

Using state for values the UI never shows costs renders; using refs for values the UI shows leaves the screen out of date.

## When to use

- Use a ref for values only handlers/effects read; state for everything rendered.

## When not to use

- Never mirror state into a ref "to avoid renders" if the UI needs the value.

## API

```ts
countRef.current += 1; // no re-render
setCount((c) => c + 1); // re-render
```

## Execution flow

1. Clicking the state counter schedules a render → new snapshot → `<Profiler>` reports a commit.
2. Clicking the ref counter mutates `current` → nothing renders.
3. "Read the ref" logs the up-to-date `current` from an event handler.

## Common mistakes

### Rendering a ref

❌ Incorrect:

```tsx
<p>Clicked {countRef.current} times</p>
```

The text only updates when something else causes a render.

✅ Correct:

```tsx
const [count, setCount] = useState(0);
<p>Clicked {count} times</p>;
```

## Edge cases

- Refs are per component instance; two mounted counters have two refs.

## Testing

The test clicks both counters three times and asserts commit counts (4 vs 1), then reads the ref from a handler and asserts the logged value is current while the ref panel still committed once.

- [`src/examples/built-in/refs/UseRefVsStateDemo.test.tsx`](../../src/examples/built-in/refs/UseRefVsStateDemo.test.tsx)

## Production considerations

- Profile before converting state to refs for performance — clarity first.
